lede: A RealNVP inside the latent code reconstructs softly on both datasets. Samples beat RealNVP and sit in the same family as the VAE.
points: VAE · normalizing flow in the latent space
title: f-VAE
question: Does a RealNVP inside the VAE latent space improve reconstruction and likelihood on digits?
process: `FVAE.forward` in `src/mnist_f_vae/model.py` draws \( z_0 \) from the encoder Gaussian, pushes it through `LatentFlow` (four affine couplings, \( y = m \odot x + (1-m) \odot (x e^{s} + t) \)), and decodes \( z_K \). `_fvae_loss` adds \( \beta \) times the Monte Carlo KL \( \log q_0(z_0|x) - \log\mathcal{N}(z_K;0,I) - \log|\det| \). Samples decode \( \mathcal{N}(0,I) \) and do not invert the flow. The flow sits in the posterior. Both datasets use latent 32, hidden 256, 4 flows, \( \beta = 1 \), and the full 60,000 / 10,000 split for 20 epochs. Digits test MSE is 0.0554, ELBO \( -69.35 \), BPD 0.953, log-det \( -12.87 \). Fashion test MSE is 0.0621, ELBO \( -65.00 \), BPD 0.945, log-det \( -9.07 \). Per-epoch curves are `loss.png` and `loss_fashion.png`. The reported BPD is the Gaussian-decoder ELBO, a different number from the RealNVP change-of-variables BPD.

opening.summary: Train and test agree on both full splits. Digit samples cover many classes and are cleaner than the RealNVP inverse grid. They are the same soft family as the vanilla VAE. The flow’s test log-det is −12.87, so the couplings change volume.
opening.hover: Hover a row for the number behind that sentence.

marks.label: Reconstruction
marks.summary: Test MSE 0.0554 and MAE 0.0920. Train is 0.0555 and 0.0923. The flowed posterior mean keeps the digit and softens the stroke. This is a full 60,000-image run at latent 32, so it is not the same setup as the latent-8 slice VAE.

marks.label: Likelihood
marks.summary: Test ELBO −69.35 and BPD 0.953, against train ELBO −69.40 and BPD 0.953. The bound held on the 10,000 test images. A Gaussian decoder can report a decent BPD while the pictures stay soft, because the likelihood averages over stroke positions.

marks.label: Flow
marks.summary: Test log-det is −12.87 and train is −12.85. The flow is not an identity at the end of training: it rescales latent volume. KL stays near 19.5 on both splits. The sample picture is still a decode of N(0, I); the inverse flow is used in the posterior, not as the gallery generator.

marks.label: Prior samples
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The 64 digit samples cover 0–9 and a few ambiguous blobs. They are cleaner than the RealNVP inverse grid, which is stroke fragments. They are softer than a sharp GAN and in the same family as the vanilla VAE samples. The vanilla VAE digits run is a 10,000-image slice at latent 8 with test MSE 0.0852. This run is the full split at latent 32 with test MSE 0.0554, so the lower error is a larger experiment, not a paired win. The gallery decodes N(0, I). The inverse flow is inside the posterior.

marks.label: Fashion-MNIST
marks.summary: Same hyperparameters, 20 epochs, full split. Test ELBO −65.00 and BPD 0.945, against train ELBO −64.33. Test MSE 0.0621 and MAE 0.1328. KL 12.95 and log-det −9.07. Prior samples read as shirts, trousers, dresses, shoes, and bags, which is clearer than the RealNVP Fashion blobs. The vanilla Fashion VAE (latent 8, slice) has test MSE 0.0749 and ELBO −71.09. The shirt logo and the thin sandal still disappear, the same failure as that VAE.
marks.frameCaption: f-VAE prior samples on Fashion-MNIST. N(0, I) through the decoder.

reflection.worked: Reconstruction and the ELBO agree between train and test on both full splits. Digit and Fashion samples cover many classes, and both grids are clearer than the RealNVP inverse samples. Fashion’s test ELBO is −65.00 against −69.35 on digits. Log-det −9.07 on Fashion and −12.87 on digits shows the couplings change volume.
reflection.unexpected: Fashion’s higher ELBO comes with a higher pixel error: test MSE 0.0621 against 0.0554 on digits. The shirt print is wiped out. The loss curve is still falling at epoch 20. Against the vanilla VAE the pictures stay in the same soft family, so the flow is not a clear visual upgrade.
reflection.why: Squared error trains the decoder to average every stroke or weave that could explain a code. A wide silhouette survives that average. A logo and a sandal strap do not. The f-VAE BPD near 0.95 and the RealNVP Fashion BPD of 3.263 are different likelihoods, so the smaller number is not a better density on the same scale. These samples never pass through the inverse flow.
reflection.improve: The Fashion loss is still descending at epoch 20, so a longer run is the next measurement. A paired comparison with the vanilla VAE needs the same split and the same latent size. Sharper prints need a different decoder likelihood. More coupling layers will not sharpen a Gaussian decoder by themselves.
